sentences.text: Titanichthys is an extinct genus of giant marine placoderms found in the shallow seas of the Late Devonian in Morocco, Eastern North America, and possibly Europe.
Titanichthys is considered the first known large-sized vertebrate filter feeder, with jaws functionally similar to those of baleen whales and basking sharks.
While Titanichthys was once estimated to reach 7 to 7.6 meters in length, a 2023 study by Engelman suggests it was likely comparable to Dunkleosteus, measuring about 4.1 meters.

When geologist Henri Termier first found fossils of Titanichthys termieri, he initially placed them in the genus Gorgonichthys before convincing colleagues they belonged to a placoderm rather than a dinosaur.
Titanichthys is assumed to have been a filter feeder that used its large mouth to swallow schools of small fish or zooplankton, retaining prey with its mouth-plates while expelling water.
Titanichthys is classified as a basal aspinothoracid, most closely related to the genera Bungartius and Tafilalichthys.
Titanichthys lived during the Eifelian to Famennian stages, approximately 393.47 to 358.86 million years ago.
